stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 6%, and then the new price is decreased by 23%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 6% increase: $100 \times (1 + 6/100) = 106.00$. After a 23% decrease on 106.00: $106.00 \times (1 - 23/100) = 81.62$. Net change $= 81.62 - 100 = -18.38\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 6 - 23 - \dfrac{138}{100} = -18.38\%$.
